result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Only the top of each page is visible in the screenshots, so I scored the sections below the fold by inference. Both answers split color into raw values and semantic roles and open with sensible principles. B's light, warm-neutral page with a teal accent and paw mark fits a calm, friendly clinic better. A has an explicit 'Change rules' section, which is a strong answer to the usage-rules item, but it renders dark and feels less warm. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Only the top of each page is visible in the screenshots, so I couldn't see either answer's samples, type and spacing scales, or most of the color work. I scored those items from what each page promises: section headings, nav links and intro text. B wins narrowly because it shows a three-tier color system (raw values, then roles, then components), principles that each give a reason, and a dedicated 'Change rules' section, which covers the usage rules better. A has a separate raw-palette and semantic-token layer and a warm, light look that suits a clinic slightly better than B's dark auto theme.
